# `missing-switch-prong`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: semantic · Profile: none · Default: error · Fixes: quick fix · Options: none

Reports a switch over a proven finite enum or tagged union that omits cases and
has no `else` prong.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

Naming every case keeps behavior synchronized when a type gains a new tag and
avoids a compiler failure at a less useful location.

## When it fires

It applies when the operand type and its cases are known, including
compiler-resolved comptime-generated named types.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
const Color = enum { red, green, blue };

fn name(c: Color) []const u8 {
    return switch (c) {
        .red => "red",
        .green => "green",
    };
}
```

Reference: <https://ziglang.org/documentation/master/#Exhaustive-Switching>
